name: Suillus luteus
notes: Long-distance exploration type [13]; native to EU and AS, invasive with pine in SA, AF and AU. Ectomycorrhizal isolates including Suillus grew 0.25 to 0.95 mm/day on agar at 22 C [25], a group figure that is not entered as this species' tip speed. Its relative S. bovinus is reported (unchecked) to be the classic species in root-window microcosms showing carbon moving between seedlings.

t_opt.note: of 24, 28 and 32 C on MMN agar, radial growth and biomass were best at 24 C (Garcia-Rodriguez et al. 2017, In vitro growth of ectomycorrhizal fungi associated with Pinus radiata plantations in Chile, Revista Fitotecnia Mexicana 40(4):415-423, https://www.redalyc.org/journal/610/61054247006/html). Nothing below 24 C was tested, so the true optimum may be lower

t_max.note: same study: mycelial biomass 28.5 mg at 24 C, 17.3 mg at 28 C and 1.9 mg at 32 C, so growth has almost stopped at 32 C; the limit is put just above it (Garcia-Rodriguez et al. 2017, https://www.redalyc.org/journal/610/61054247006/html)

tip_speed.source: Gonzalez M., Quiroz I., Travieso R., Chung P., Garcia E. 2015, Determinacion de medios de cultivo y pH para la masificacion in vitro de cepas de Suillus luteus Aubl. asociadas a Pinus radiata D. Don y Scleroderma citrinum Pers. asociadas a Eucalyptus globulus Labill. de la region del Biobio, Chile, Revista Arvore 39(1):105-113
tip_speed.note: mean growth rate on MMN agar 0.59 +/- 0.17 mm/day (Table 2; three Chilean strains, three pH levels, 23 C, 38 days, rate from a linear fit of radial growth); 0.59 x 41.7 = 25 um/h. Strain means 0.56 to 0.69 and single treatments 0.32 to 0.87 mm/day (13 to 36 um/h). 23 C is close to the 24 C taken as the optimum, so no correction. This is growth on agar without a host; rhizomorphs in soil with a pine may extend faster

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found
